A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSSA/LSSAR research work. All 11 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v3 were readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 training experiments on fineweb-10B, attention comparisons, normalization ablations, and reweighting sensitivity results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds zero-shot downstream evaluations of Softmax and LSSAR in Section 3.5 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The LSSA/LSSAR computations in Equations (3)–(5) retain query/key normalization, length scaling, Softplus, masking, power reweighting, and row normalization. The first-three-row exception is also retained. Describing reweighting as architectural introduces no new computational step.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates language modeling on fineweb-10B. v3 retains this coverage and adds ARC-E/ARC-C, HellaSwag, PIQA, MMLU, SciQ, and SummScreen, substantially extending evaluation to question answering, reasoning, continuation selection, and summarization.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the same activation variants and Softmax, Sigmoid, and ReLU comparators, including their reweighted variants. 'Sigmoid (Proposed)' becomes 'Sigmoid (Tab. 3).' The new downstream comparison uses the existing Softmax baseline; newly cited positional-scaling approaches are not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 3.5 adds a distinct zero-shot evaluation protocol using normalized accuracy, MMLU accuracy, and SummScreen ROUGE-1, with summarization contexts up to 2K tokens. Original model and training budgets remain unchanged. v3 specifies Dynamic NTK Scaling where v1 said NTK Scaling, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The attention-sign and normalization experiments, component ablations, activation comparisons, and reweighting analyses are retained. Figure 2 preserves the p sweep across 1K–16K contexts, including p = 50 and 100. No new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new downstream table follows the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the plotted findings are retained, while Table 5 adds substantial downstream results. LSSAR wins five columns, ties MMLU at 22.97, and loses ARC-C, 22.61 versus Softmax's 23.72. SummScreen ROUGE-1 is 6.309 versus 1.682. These are new within-v3 comparisons, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 relaxes the stated exponent requirement from a positive integer to a positive scalar hyperparameter. Otherwise, the Softmax decomposition and asymptotic sharpening argument remain unchanged. Moving v1's Equation (6) inline and renumbering Equation (7) do not introduce a new proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about normalization, LSSA, numerical stability, and 16-fold length extrapolation remain. v3 adds explicit claims of superior downstream and real-world task performance to the abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the SummScreen result as evidence of information synthesis across 2K-token contexts and more explicitly argues that reweighting addresses attention smoothing beyond positional adjustments. Existing small-model, maximum-length, scaling-factor, and computational-cost limitations remain; the depth analogy is expanded.

D1.justification: v3 identifies lm-evaluation-harness and specifically names Dynamic NTK Scaling. It removes v1's explicit source-code URL and direct FineWeb dataset footnote, adding a FineWeb paper citation instead. Hardware and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged. The missing code link does not establish that the code itself was withdrawn.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work add explicit positioning against post-hoc positional interpolation and NTK adjustments. References are added for scaling resources, FineWeb, downstream benchmarks, the evaluation harness, and DeepSeek-R1. The existing discussion of Softmax-free attention remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 revises parts of the introduction and conclusion, reorganizes the contribution bullets, adds Section 3.5, and expands the depth analogy. Terminology, affiliations, and citation style are edited, while the six-section organization and most existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with text wrapping around several equations and Table 2. Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated, plot colors and backgrounds change, and Table 5 is added. Figures 1–2 redisplay the retained results.

improvement.justification: Section 3.5 and Table 5 address v1's reliance on language-model validation loss by testing downstream usefulness and revealing task-specific limits, including the ARC-C loss and MMLU tie. This strengthens empirical relevance. The gain remains limited by unchanged small-model coverage and absent uncertainty reporting, while removal of the explicit code link weakens reproducibility disclosure.
